newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end firm on foreign buy orders.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end firm on foreign buy orders.

text.p: Chilean blue chips reversed early losses to close higher in modest trade with the market boosted by foreign interest in stocks including telecom CTC, said dealers.
The bolsa is expected to open firmer, although the tempo is likely to be set by Wall Street's opening mood, they said.
"I think it will be slightly positive, but much depends on what foreign investors do," said one dealer.
The 40-share index ended up 0.88 percent at 115.28 points. The general index gained 0.71 percent at 5,318.92 points amid volume of 11.7 billion pesos.
Most of the local buy orders were from private players, with institutional investors remaining on the sidelines.
Winners included CTC, which climbed on confidence that the company will outperform rivals in Chile's highly competitive telecommunications market, said traders.
"The general view is that CTC has better possibilities of developing its business than Entel," said one dealer.
CTC closed up 2.12 percent at 2,800 pesos. Entel, Chile's largest long-distance carrier, rose 0.34 percent to 2,940 pesos.
Losers included financial group Security, down 3.7 percent to 385 pesos, and fertilizer-maker Soquimich, which shed 0.84 percent to 2,360 pesos.
